body:
## Note on f7085a9 (queue-phase rejection)

The rejection is valid, and checking queue stability separately from endpoints is the right fix. One observation and one suggestion for the next prospectively frozen confirmation.

**The four OFF samples match your scale table.** Point scoring calls the ~162ms samples a large miss, but they sit only 11–16ms from the model's own next boundary.

| OFF sample | Matching scale in your table | Error vs. model point (6.698ms) | Error vs. nearest model boundary (6.698 or 175.183ms) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 160.867ms (ct-069) | ≤0.98 (163.7ms) | 154.2ms | 14.3ms |
| 163.909ms (ct-107) | ≤0.98 | 157.2ms | 11.3ms |
| 20.398ms (ct-086) | ~1.03 (18.9ms) | 13.7ms | 13.7ms |
| 23.010ms (ct-118) | ~1.03 | 16.3ms | 16.3ms |

The model's 175.183ms is its next commit at 575.183ms minus the 400ms arrival.

- **OFF runs:** they behave like a ±2–3% effective-clock spread around the frozen law.
- **LIGHT runs:** their ADD times (404–410ms) sit within about ±1% of the model.

A 400ms arrival 6.7ms ahead of a predicted boundary falls inside the OFF spread, so queue residence there is bimodal, and no point prediction can pass a point budget. The late branch fits the existing 20% budget. The early branch misses the 10ms floor by 4–6ms, consistent with the ~12ms same-phase OFF/LIGHT shift below.

**Suggestion: preregister a phase-margin check before the next fresh run, using calibration evidence only.**

1. For each held arrival, find whether the consumed iteration flips when all coefficients scale within ±s. Set s from calibration-only OFF repeat or effective-clock spread; it must not come from held data.
2. If a flip occurs, mark that cell's queue residence `phase_ambiguous`. Predict both branches (`r_early`, `r_late`), score each sample against its nearest branch with the existing per-branch budget, and report branch counts. Endpoint/TTFT scoring is unchanged.
3. If no flip occurs, keep point scoring.

Alternatively, move held arrival offsets to mid-interval for the fresh confirmation, again decided before collection.

**Reporting the new guard's failures.** `queue_quality` failures currently feed `quality.passed`, so a run is rejected. That treats three different situations the same way:

- **Phase-ambiguous cells:** if the frozen model predicts a cell is phase-ambiguous, a spread failure is expected and is not evidence against the model. As written, the guard will likely reject the next run at the same offsets whatever the model does.
- **Same-phase observer shifts:** the paired OFF/LIGHT check also fails without any phase change. ct-086/085 differ by 11.8ms and ct-118/117 by 12.7ms, against the 10ms limit.
- **Real model error:** this is the only case that should count against the model.

Reporting these three separately would keep a rejection informative.
